Only the order in which *independent* elements are visited\n// changes, so results are bit-identical to the sequential version.\n\nnamespace {\n\n// Blocking parameters for the C = X * Y^T kernel below.\nconstexpr size_t GEMM_KC = 256; // k block (packed panel stays in L2)\nconstexpr size_t GEMM_NC = 128; // column block\nconstexpr size_t GEMM_MR = 4;   // micro-kernel rows\nconstexpr size_t GEMM_NR = 8;   // micro-kernel columns\n\nconstexpr size_t CHOL_NB = 64; // Cholesky panel width\n\n// C[i][j] = sum_{k=0}^{K-1} X[i][k] * Y[j][k], accumulated in ascending k order.\n// C is overwritten (its previous contents are ignored). Rows of C are distributed\n// over the threads, so the routine contains no barrier at all.\nvoid gemm_nt(const double* __restrict X, const size_t ldx, const double* __restrict Y, const size_t ldy,\n             double* __restrict C, const size_t ldc, const size_t M, const size_t N, const size_t K) {\n    #pragma omp parallel\n    {\n        const size_t nthreads = (size_t)omp_get_num_threads();\n        const size_t tid = (size_t)omp_get_thread_num();\n\n        // Static, evenly balanced row distribution.\n        const size_t base = M / nthreads;\n        const size_t rem = M % nthreads;\n        const size_t i0 = tid * base + std::min(tid, rem);\n        const size_t i1 = i0 + base + (tid < rem ? 1 : 0);\n\n        for (size_t i = i0; Rows of C are distributed\n// over the threads, so the routine contains no barrier at all.\nvoid gemm_nt(const double* __restrict X, const size_t ldx, const double* __restrict Y, const size_t ldy,\n             double* __restrict C, const size_t ldc, const size_t M, const size_t N, const size_t K) {\n    #pragma omp parallel\n    {\n        const size_t nthreads = (size_t)omp_get_num_threads();\n        const size_t tid = (size_t)omp_get_thread_num();\n\n        // Static, evenly balanced row distribution.\n        const size_t base = M / nthreads;\n        const size_t rem = M % nthreads;\n        const size_t i0 = tid * base + std::min(tid, rem);\n        const size_t i1 = i0 + base + (tid < rem ? 1 : 0);\n\n        for (size_t i = i0; Rows of C are distributed\n// over the threads, so the routine contains no barrier at all.\nvoid gemm_nt(const double* __restrict X, const size_t ldx, const double* __restrict Y, const size_t ldy,\n             double* __restrict C, const size_t ldc, const size_t M, const size_t N, const size_t K) {\n    #pragma omp parallel\n    {\n        const size_t nthreads = (size_t)omp_get_num_threads();\n        const size_t tid = (size_t)omp_get_thread_num();\n\n        // Static, evenly balanced row distribution.\n        const size_t base = M / nthreads;\n        const size_t rem = M % nthreads;\n        const size_t i0 = tid * base + std::min(tid, rem);\n        const size_t i1 = i0 + base + (tid < rem ? 1 : 0);\n\n        for (size_t i = i0; i < i1; ++i) {\n            std::fill_n(C + i * ldc, N, 0.0);\n        }\n\n        if (K > 0 && i1 > i0) {\n            std::vector<double> pack(GEMM_NC * GEMM_KC);\n\n            for (size_t jc = 0; jc < N; jc += GEMM_NC) {\n                const size_t nc = std::min(GEMM_NC, N - jc);\n\n                for (size_t kb = 0; kb < K; kb += GEMM_KC) {\n                    const size_t kc = std::min(GEMM_KC, K - kb);\n\n                    // Pack Y into k-major strips of GEMM_NR columns so that the\n                    // micro-kernel can vectorize over columns while k stays sequential.\n                    for (size_t js = 0; js < nc; js += GEMM_NR) {\n                        const size_t nr = std::min(GEMM_NR, nc - js);\n                        double* __restrict p = pack.data() + js * kc;\n                        for (size_t kk = 0; j0 < n; j0 += CHOL_NB) {\n        const size_t nb = std::min(CHOL_NB, n - j0);\n        const size_t m = n - j0;\n\n        // Left-looking update of the panel: everything that the columns of this\n        // panel owe to the already factored columns [0, j0).\n        gemm_nt(a + j0 * n, n, a + j0 * n, n, S.data(), nb, m, nb, j0);\n\n        // Factor the nb x nb diagonal block (tiny, kept sequential).\n        for (size_t jj = 0; jj < nb; ++jj) {\n            const size_t j = j0 + jj;\n\n            double sum = S[jj * nb + jj];\n            for (size_t k = j0; k < j; ++k) {\n                sum += a[j * n + k] * a[j * n + k];\n            }\n            const double val = a[j * n + j] - sum;\n            if (val <= 0.0) {\n                // Matrix is not positive definite\n                printf(\"Error: Matrix is not positive definite at diagonal element %zu\\n\", j);\n                return false;\n            }\n            const double diag = sqrt(val);\n            a[j * n + j] = diag;\n\n            for (size_t ii = jj + 1; jj < nb; ++jj) {\n            const size_t j = j0 + jj;\n\n            double sum = S[jj * nb + jj];\n            for (size_t k = j0; k < j; ++k) {\n                sum += a[j * n + k] * a[j * n + k];\n            }\n            const double val = a[j * n + j] - sum;\n            if (val <= 0.0) {\n                // Matrix is not positive definite\n                printf(\"Error: Matrix is not positive definite at diagonal element %zu\\n\", j);\n                return false;\n            }\n            const double diag = sqrt(val);\n            a[j * n + j] = diag;\n\n            for (size_t ii = jj + 1; ii < nb; ++ii) {\n                const size_t i = j0 + ii;\n                double s = S[ii * nb + jj];\n                for (size_t k = j0; k < j; ++k) {\n                    s += a[i * n + k] * a[j * n + k];\n                }\n                a[i * n + j] = (a[i * n + j] - s) / diag;\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Remaining rows of the panel: fully independent across rows.\n        #pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n        for (size_t i = j0 + nb; {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CegVwdhS7Sttfmuo3zAdY","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The Cholesky benchmark is now parallelized with OpenMP, and it produces **bit-identical output to the original** at every matrix size I tested.\n\n## What changed (`cholesky/cholesky.cpp`, `cholesky/CMakeLists.txt`)\n\n**Algorithm.** The unblocked row-by-row factorization became a blocked *left-looking* one: for each 64-column panel, the accumulated contribution of all previously factored columns is computed by a blocked `C = X·Yᵀ` kernel, then the small diagonal block is factored (sequentially — it's ~5% of the work) and the remaining rows are finished in one fully independent parallel loop. The same kernel also replaced the O(n³) loops in `generatePositiveDefiniteMatrix` and `validateCholesky`, which otherwise dominated wall time.\n\n**Kernel.** A packed, register-blocked AVX2 micro-kernel (4×8 tile, accumulators in `ymm` registers, column panel packed k-major per thread so it stays in the core's L2).\n\n**Threading.** Threads are pinned one per physical core, and the team size is fixed once at startup. Two things mattered a lot here: unpinned threads cost ~3x, and letting the team size vary between regions cost ~8x (libgomp re-creates workers, which inherit the master's affinity mask).\n\n## Equivalent semantics\nEvery output element is still one sequential dot product over ascending `k`; only the order in which independent elements are visited changed. To also match the *rounding*, the kernel reproduces what gcc does with the original loop — a packed multiply with separately rounded products, plus a `std::fma` epilogue for the final `K % 4` terms. I verified `Sum`/`Min`/`Max`/`Sample`/`Hash` against the original binary for n = 1…40, 63, 100, 255, 256, 511, 512, 777, 1000, 1023, 1024, 2048: all identical, and independent of thread count and binding.\n\n## Performance (GFLOPS as the benchmark reports them)\n\n| n | original | parallel | speedup |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 512 | 1.54 | 44.7 | 29x |\n| 1024 | 1.42 | 89.5 | 63x |\n| 2048 | 1.35 | 260 | 193x |\n| 4096 | — | 460 | — |\n| 8192 | — | ~1020 | ~760x (est.) |\n\nOne caveat worth stating: the bit-exactness relies on matching this gcc version's vectorization split.
